In EXP-001 (primary cell) MMR re-ranking recovered part of the entropy loss of similarity ranking (MMR minus similarity +0.2147, 95% t [0.2125, 0.2169]) and popularity changed H_exp by only -0.0089 [-0.0115, -0.0064], below the smallest effect of interest, while raising item-exposure Gini by 0.7308.

text: The EXP-002 drift-form rule was not met: D under additive-then-clip was -0.4363 (alpha_0 1.0) and -0.4351 (alpha_0 0.1), same sign and above 0.05 in size. The check is weak: for non-negative p, additive-then-clip followed by normalisation equals the multiplicative rule with gamma/(1+gamma) unless the clip binds.
status: supported as measured; limited construct value (limitations 12)
limitations: near-reparametrisation, not an independent drift form

text: With a Zipf-skewed catalog the similarity-minus-random H_exp contrast was -0.5060 (tau 0.1, 95% t [-0.5169, -0.4951]) and -0.5365 (tau 0.3, [-0.5469, -0.5260]); neither the skew nor the sharpness invalidation criterion of EXP-003 was met, and no sign reversal occurred.
limitations: the exploratory reversal seen before the freeze under midpoint 0.5 did not recur under the frozen calibration

text: The similarity-minus-random H_exp reduction was larger under the Zipf catalog than under the uniform catalog: interaction -0.1059 (tau 0.1, Welch 95% [-0.1170, -0.0948]) and -0.1503 (tau 0.3, [-0.1611, -0.1396]).

With MovieLens 1M held-out-half preference vectors and catalog topic weights, similarity ranking lowered H_exp relative to random by 0.4095 (95% t [-0.4210, -0.3980], 20 seeds); H1 supported, contradiction rule not met, no sign reversal.
scope: simulation with MovieLens-derived inputs; not a claim about MovieLens users
